# pay-first

Synthetic rows, each one description, built from the L2 rule and its notes in
`docs/design/drafts/too-good-to-be-true.md` §2.2:

1. A deposit to hold counts whatever the balance terms (the Which? deposit case).
2. "Can't do in person" is a negated exclusion; "before I post" is a before-cue.
3. Bare "bank transfer only" is never enough.
4. Row 1 of the recorded run: payment tied to the pickup is excluded, and is the X1 counter fact.
5. Friends and family counts at any time.
6. "No deposit" is negated; the pay-on-collection fact still fires.
7. Digit-for-letter spellings (3→e, 0→o) match.
8. BT counts only inside a payment clause (it is also the Northern Ireland postcode area).
9. "First come first served" is no before-cue.
10. A clause that also demands a deposit is pay-first, never payment on collection.
11. "Payment first" is a before-cue.
12. Gift cards count at any time.
